title: Water (H₂O) — Why is Water Bent?
description: Discover why the water molecule is bent at 104.5° instead of being linear like CO₂.

steps.prompt: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons and shares 2 with hydrogens. What shape do you predict water forms?
steps.explanation: Correct! Oxygen has 2 bonded pairs and 2 non-bonding lone pairs. The lone pairs exert strong electrostatic repulsion, pushing the H-O-H bond angle down from tetrahedral 109.5° to 104.5°.

steps.prompt: Grab a hydrogen atom with your closed fist and stretch the O-H bond. Observe how potential energy increases as you pull against the bond spring.
steps.explanation: Great work! Chemical bonds act like quantum harmonic springs: pulling them increases potential strain energy V(r), which pulls the atom back to its rest length (0.96 Å) upon release.

steps.prompt: According to VSEPR theory, which electron repulsion is strongest in water?
steps.explanation: Lone Pair – Lone Pair repulsion is the strongest because lone pairs are held by only one atomic nucleus and occupy greater spatial volume.
